ja: 当てにする、頼りにする
en: to rely on something happening or on someone doing something
ex: We were banking on good weather, so the sudden storm ruined our plans for the outdoor festival.
exJa: 好天を当てにしていたので、突然の嵐で野外フェスの計画が台無しになった。

en: to dismiss or ignore something or someone in a casual, uninterested way
ex: The minister brushed off questions about the scandal, insisting that reporters focus on the new budget.
exJa: 大臣はスキャンダルについての質問を一蹴し、記者たちに新予算に注目するよう求めた。

en: to give money or help along with other people; to add a remark
ex: Everyone in the office chipped in to buy a farewell gift for the retiring manager.
exJa: 退職する部長への送別の贈り物を買うため、職場の全員がお金を出し合った。

ja: 大量生産する、量産する
en: to produce large amounts of something quickly, often without care for quality
ex: The studio churns out a dozen formulaic action movies every year, each one less original than the last.
exJa: そのスタジオは毎年ありきたりのアクション映画を十数本量産しており、どれも前作より独創性に欠ける。

en: to defend yourself against an attack, criticism, or unwanted questions
ex: The small company managed to fend off a hostile takeover bid from its much larger rival.
exJa: その小さな会社は、はるかに大きなライバル企業からの敵対的買収をなんとか退けた。

ja: （問題などを）取り繕う、ごまかす
en: to avoid dealing with a problem or mistake by treating it as unimportant
ex: The annual report glossed over the factory accidents and devoted pages to the company's charity work.
exJa: 年次報告書は工場の事故を軽く扱い、会社の慈善活動に何ページも割いていた。

ja: （合意などを）苦労してまとめる
en: to reach an agreement or solution after long and difficult discussion
ex: Negotiators worked through the night to hammer out a ceasefire agreement acceptable to both sides.
exJa: 交渉担当者たちは双方が受け入れられる停戦合意をまとめるため、夜通し協議した。

en: to solve small problems or difficulties so things work smoothly
ex: We still need to iron out a few technical glitches before the app is released to the public.
exJa: アプリを一般公開する前に、いくつかの技術的な不具合を解消する必要がある。

ja: 激しく非難する、食ってかかる
en: to suddenly attack someone with words or physical force
ex: Exhausted and frustrated, he lashed out at his colleagues over a minor mistake in the report.
exJa: 疲れ果てて苛立っていた彼は、報告書の小さなミスのことで同僚に食ってかかった。

ja: 熟考する、じっくり考える
en: to think carefully about something for a period of time
ex: She spent the weekend mulling over the job offer before finally deciding to stay in Osaka.
exJa: 彼女は週末の間その仕事のオファーについてじっくり考え、最終的に大阪に残ることにした。

en: to develop or turn out in a particular way, especially successfully
ex: His plan to open a café didn't pan out, so he went back to his old job at the bank.
exJa: カフェを開く計画はうまくいかず、彼は銀行の元の仕事に戻った。

en: to earn large amounts of money, often easily
ex: The blockbuster raked in over 200 million dollars in its opening weekend alone.
exJa: その大ヒット映画は公開初週末だけで2億ドル以上を稼ぎ出した。

ja: すらすらと言う、まくし立てる
en: to say a list or series of things quickly and from memory
ex: The waiter rattled off a long list of daily specials before we had even opened the menu.
exJa: 私たちがメニューを開く前に、ウェイターは本日のおすすめ料理を長々とすらすら述べた。

ja: なんとか暮らしていく
en: to manage to live with very little money
ex: As a student, he scraped by on instant noodles and a part-time job at a convenience store.
exJa: 学生時代、彼はインスタントラーメンとコンビニのアルバイトでなんとか食いつないだ。

en: to prevent something bad from happening, or to delay it
ex: The government cut interest rates in a desperate attempt to stave off a recession.
exJa: 政府は景気後退を食い止めようと、必死の思いで金利を引き下げた。

en: to help someone through a difficult period, especially by lending money
ex: My sister lent me enough money to tide me over until my first paycheck arrived.
exJa: 姉は初任給が入るまでしのげるだけのお金を貸してくれた。

en: to avoid a duty or promise in a dishonest or cowardly way
ex: He tried to weasel out of paying his share of the bill by claiming he had forgotten his wallet.
exJa: 彼は財布を忘れたと言って、自分の分の勘定を払うのをずるく逃れようとした。

en: to stir up strong feelings in people; to make food quickly
ex: The candidate whipped up anger among voters by blaming immigrants for the country's problems.
exJa: その候補者は国の問題を移民のせいにして、有権者の怒りをあおった。

en: to avoid doing something you should do by making clever excuses
ex: No matter how hard she tries, she won't be able to wriggle out of attending the shareholders' meeting.
exJa: どんなに頑張っても、彼女は株主総会への出席を逃れることはできないだろう。

en: to rescue a person or organization from financial trouble
ex: Taxpayers were furious when the government spent billions to bail out the failing banks.
exJa: 政府が経営難の銀行を救済するために数十億を費やしたとき、納税者は激怒した。

en: to withdraw from an activity or position, especially gracefully
ex: After forty years on stage, the veteran actor decided to bow out with one final performance.
exJa: 40年間舞台に立ったベテラン俳優は、最後の公演をもって引退することにした。

en: to rudely interrupt a conversation or interfere in something
ex: I was trying to explain the situation to my boss when a coworker butted in with his own opinion.
exJa: 上司に状況を説明しようとしていたら、同僚が自分の意見で割り込んできた。

ja: 屈服する、折れる、崩れ落ちる
en: to finally agree to something after being pressured; to collapse inward
ex: After weeks of protests, the management caved in and agreed to the workers' demands.
exJa: 数週間の抗議の末、経営陣は折れて労働者の要求に応じた。

en: to start dealing much more strictly with illegal or unwanted behavior
ex: The authorities are cracking down on websites that sell counterfeit designer goods to unsuspecting shoppers.
exJa: 当局は何も知らない買い物客に偽ブランド品を販売するウェブサイトの取り締まりを強化している。

en: to take advantage of a situation to make money or gain something
ex: Souvenir shops quickly cashed in on the popularity of the anime by selling unofficial merchandise.
exJa: 土産物店はそのアニメの人気に便乗し、非公式グッズを売ってすぐに儲けた。

ja: （勝利などを）収める、～のせいにする
en: to achieve a success or score; to say that something is caused by something else
ex: The team chalked up its tenth consecutive victory with a dramatic goal in the final minute.
exJa: チームは最後の1分の劇的なゴールで10連勝を挙げた。

ja: 思い起こさせる、（魔法のように）出す
en: to bring an image or memory into someone's mind; to produce as if by magic
ex: The smell of fresh bread always conjures up memories of my grandmother's kitchen.
exJa: 焼きたてのパンの匂いは、いつも祖母の台所の記憶を呼び起こす。

en: to stop people entering an area by surrounding it with police or barriers
ex: Police cordoned off the street while bomb disposal experts examined the suspicious package.
exJa: 爆発物処理の専門家が不審な包みを調べる間、警察は通りを封鎖した。

en: to give out money, food, or advice in small amounts to many people
ex: Volunteers doled out bowls of hot soup to the people waiting in line outside the shelter.
exJa: ボランティアたちは避難所の外に並ぶ人々に温かいスープを配った。

en: to give out criticism, advice, or punishment freely; to serve food
ex: He loves to dish out criticism, but he can't take it when others point out his own mistakes.
exJa: 彼は人を批判するのは大好きだが、他人に自分のミスを指摘されると耐えられない。

ja: くよくよ考える、こだわる
en: to keep thinking or talking about something, especially something unpleasant
ex: There's no point dwelling on your failed exam; focus on preparing for the next one instead.
exJa: 不合格だった試験のことをくよくよ考えても仕方ない。代わりに次の試験の準備に集中しよう。

ja: けしかける、そそのかす
en: to encourage someone to do something, usually something foolish or risky
ex: Egged on by his friends, he jumped off the bridge into the freezing river.
exJa: 友人たちにけしかけられて、彼は橋から凍えるような川に飛び込んだ。

en: to manage to make a living or obtain something with great difficulty
ex: Farmers in the region eke out a living by growing rice on small, terraced fields.
exJa: その地域の農民は小さな棚田で米を育て、かろうじて生計を立てている。

en: to waste time or money on unimportant things
ex: He frittered away his inheritance on expensive cars and gambling trips to Las Vegas.
exJa: 彼は相続した遺産を高級車やラスベガスへのギャンブル旅行で浪費した。

en: to make someone accept an excuse or something inferior instead of what they want
ex: When I complained about the broken heater, the landlord tried to fob me off with vague promises.
exJa: 壊れたヒーターについて苦情を言うと、大家は曖昧な約束で私をごまかそうとした。

en: to hide or stay in a place, often to avoid people or danger
ex: The suspect holed up in an abandoned warehouse for three days before surrendering to police.
exJa: 容疑者は警察に投降するまで3日間、廃倉庫に立てこもった。

en: to prevent information about something bad from becoming public
ex: The company tried to hush up the data leak, but a former employee revealed it to the press.
exJa: 会社はデータ流出をもみ消そうとしたが、元従業員が報道機関に明かした。

en: to become very interested in an idea and seize on it eagerly
ex: The media latched onto the senator's careless remark and repeated it for weeks.
exJa: メディアはその上院議員の不用意な発言に飛びつき、何週間も繰り返し報じた。

en: to turn the pages of a book or magazine quickly, reading only parts
ex: While waiting for the dentist, I leafed through an old magazine full of celebrity gossip.
exJa: 歯医者を待つ間、芸能ゴシップだらけの古い雑誌をぱらぱらとめくった。

en: to give someone a punishment or harsh treatment
ex: The judge meted out the harshest possible sentence to discourage similar crimes in the future.
exJa: 裁判官は今後の同様の犯罪を抑止するため、可能な限り最も重い刑を言い渡した。

en: to manage to do something without much skill, planning, or knowledge
ex: None of us spoke much Italian, but we muddled through with gestures and a phrasebook.
exJa: 私たちの誰もイタリア語はあまり話せなかったが、身振りと会話帳でなんとか乗り切った。

ja: うとうとする、居眠りする
en: to fall asleep, especially without meaning to
ex: The lecture was so dull that half the students nodded off before the professor finished.
exJa: 講義があまりに退屈だったので、教授が話し終える前に学生の半分が居眠りした。

en: to admit that you have done something wrong
ex: Nobody would own up to breaking the printer, so the manager asked everyone to be more careful.
exJa: 誰もプリンターを壊したことを認めなかったので、部長は全員にもっと気をつけるよう求めた。

en: to decide not to take advantage of an opportunity
ex: She passed up a chance to study in London because she didn't want to leave her ailing father.
exJa: 病気の父のもとを離れたくなかったので、彼女はロンドン留学の機会を見送った。

ja: 次第に消える、先細りになる
en: to gradually become smaller or weaker and then end
ex: The protest began with thousands of people but petered out as the rain grew heavier.
exJa: 抗議活動は数千人で始まったが、雨が強まるにつれて次第に下火になった。

en: to gradually stop using or providing something
ex: The city plans to phase out plastic shopping bags over the next three years.
exJa: 市は今後3年間でレジ袋を段階的に廃止する計画だ。

ja: 熟読する、丹念に調べる
en: to study or read something very carefully and for a long time
ex: Investigators pored over thousands of documents looking for evidence of fraud.
exJa: 捜査官たちは詐欺の証拠を求めて何千もの書類を丹念に調べた。

ja: 下支えする、てこ入れする
en: to support something that would otherwise fail or fall
ex: The central bank bought government bonds in an effort to prop up the collapsing currency.
exJa: 中央銀行は暴落する通貨を下支えしようと国債を購入した。

ja: 抑制する、歯止めをかける
en: to control or limit something more strictly
ex: The new CEO promised to rein in spending after years of reckless expansion.
exJa: 新CEOは長年の無謀な拡大の後、支出を抑制すると約束した。

en: to find and completely remove something bad
ex: The new police chief vowed to root out corruption within the department.
exJa: 新任の警察署長は署内の汚職を根絶すると誓った。

ja: （手伝いに）引き入れる、巻き込む
en: to persuade someone to help with an activity, often when they do not want to
ex: My aunt roped in all her nephews to help move furniture into her new apartment.
exJa: 叔母は甥っ子全員を巻き込んで、新しいアパートへの家具の運び込みを手伝わせた。

ja: （食事などを）手早く用意する
en: to make or find something quickly using whatever is available
ex: There wasn't much in the fridge, but she managed to rustle up a tasty omelet for us.
exJa: 冷蔵庫にはあまり物がなかったが、彼女は手早くおいしいオムレツを作ってくれた。

en: to pay a lot of money for something, often unwillingly
ex: Fans shelled out hundreds of dollars for tickets to the band's reunion concert.
exJa: ファンはそのバンドの再結成コンサートのチケットに何百ドルも払った。

en: to choose one person or thing from a group for special praise or criticism
ex: The coach singled out the young goalkeeper for praise after the team's narrow victory.
exJa: 監督はチームの辛勝後、若いゴールキーパーを名指しで称賛した。

en: to take money dishonestly from a fund or business over a period of time
ex: The treasurer siphoned off millions from the charity's accounts over a decade.
exJa: 会計係は10年にわたり慈善団体の口座から数百万を横領していた。

ja: 先を争って買う、飛びつく
en: to buy or take something quickly and eagerly
ex: Bargain hunters snapped up the discounted televisions within minutes of the store opening.
exJa: 開店から数分のうちに、掘り出し物を狙う客が値引きされたテレビを買い占めた。

en: to talk to someone in order to find out their opinions or intentions
ex: Before announcing the merger, the CEO quietly sounded out several major shareholders.
exJa: 合併を発表する前に、CEOは主要株主数人の意向を密かに打診した。

ja: 詳しく説明する、明確にする
en: to explain something clearly and in detail
ex: The contract spells out exactly what happens if either party fails to meet the deadline.
exJa: 契約書には、どちらかが期限を守れなかった場合にどうなるかが明確に記されている。

en: to spend a lot of money on something enjoyable
ex: For their anniversary, they splashed out on a weekend at a luxury hot spring resort.
exJa: 結婚記念日に、二人は奮発して高級温泉旅館で週末を過ごした。

en: to end something harmful by taking strong action
ex: The government launched a nationwide campaign to stamp out drunk driving during the holiday season.
exJa: 政府は休暇シーズン中の飲酒運転を撲滅するため、全国的なキャンペーンを開始した。

en: to store something in a secret or safe place
ex: The old man had stashed away thousands of dollars in coffee cans buried in his garden.
exJa: 老人は庭に埋めたコーヒー缶に何千ドルも隠し持っていた。

en: to support or defend someone who is being criticized or attacked
ex: When the other kids teased me at school, my older brother always stuck up for me.
exJa: 学校で他の子たちにからかわれると、兄はいつも私をかばってくれた。

en: to cause trouble, argument, or strong feelings
ex: The documentary stirred up a heated debate about animal testing in the cosmetics industry.
exJa: そのドキュメンタリーは化粧品業界の動物実験をめぐる激しい議論を巻き起こした。

en: to strongly believe that something is effective and recommend it
ex: My grandmother swears by ginger tea as a cure for colds and refuses to take medicine.
exJa: 祖母は風邪にはショウガ茶が効くと信じ込んでいて、薬を飲もうとしない。

ja: 不正に手を加える、細工する
en: to interfere with something in order to damage or secretly alter it
ex: Investigators found evidence that someone had tampered with the brakes before the crash.
exJa: 捜査官は事故前に何者かがブレーキに細工していた証拠を見つけた。

en: to make use of a source of energy, knowledge, or a market
ex: The startup hopes to tap into the growing demand for plant-based foods among young consumers.
exJa: そのスタートアップは若い消費者の間で高まる植物性食品の需要を取り込みたいと考えている。

ja: 酷評する、激しく非難する
en: to criticize someone or something very severely
ex: The critics tore into the director's latest film, calling it a bloated and confusing mess.
exJa: 批評家たちは監督の最新作を酷評し、冗長で分かりにくい駄作だと評した。

en: to secretly warn someone or give information to the police
ex: An anonymous caller tipped off the police about a drug deal taking place at the harbor.
exJa: 匿名の電話の主が、港で行われている麻薬取引について警察に密告した。

en: to cause a sudden violent or difficult situation
ex: The arrest of the popular opposition leader touched off riots in several major cities.
exJa: 人気野党指導者の逮捕は、いくつかの主要都市で暴動を引き起こした。

en: to mark or cause the beginning of something new
ex: The invention of the smartphone ushered in a new era of constant connectivity.
exJa: スマートフォンの発明は常時接続の新時代の幕開けとなった。

en: to say that you believe someone is honest or that something is true
ex: I've worked with him for ten years, so I can vouch for his honesty and reliability.
exJa: 彼とは10年一緒に働いてきたので、彼の誠実さと信頼性は私が保証できる。

en: to prevent something harmful, such as illness or danger, from affecting you
ex: Many people believe that eating garlic helps ward off colds during the winter months.
exJa: 冬の間ニンニクを食べると風邪の予防になると信じている人は多い。

ja: 骨抜きにする、（液体を）薄める
en: to make a plan, law, or statement weaker or less effective
ex: Under pressure from industry lobbyists, lawmakers watered down the proposed environmental regulations.
exJa: 業界ロビイストの圧力を受け、議員たちは環境規制案を骨抜きにした。

en: to gradually disappear or stop having an effect
ex: When the anesthetic began to wear off, she felt a sharp pain in her jaw.
exJa: 麻酔が切れ始めると、彼女はあごに鋭い痛みを感じた。

ja: ふるい落とす、取り除く
en: to remove unwanted or weak members or things from a group
ex: The first round of interviews is designed to weed out applicants who lack basic skills.
exJa: 一次面接は基本的なスキルに欠ける応募者をふるい落とすためのものだ。

en: to gradually reduce the size or number of something
ex: The committee whittled down the list of two hundred candidates to just five finalists.
exJa: 委員会は200人の候補者リストを最終候補の5人にまで絞り込んだ。

ja: 徐々に縮小する、くつろぐ
en: to gradually reduce activity before stopping completely; to relax
ex: The company began to wind down its operations in Russia after sanctions were imposed.
exJa: 制裁が科された後、その会社はロシアでの事業を段階的に縮小し始めた。

en: to eat food very quickly and in large amounts
ex: The hungry boy wolfed down three bowls of curry before anyone else had finished one.
exJa: 腹ペコの少年は、他の誰かが1杯食べ終える前にカレーを3杯平らげた。

ja: 見限る、（負債を）帳消しにする
en: to decide someone or something will fail or is worthless; to cancel a debt
ex: Many critics had written off the veteran boxer, but he won the title in stunning fashion.
exJa: 多くの評論家がそのベテランボクサーを見限っていたが、彼は見事にタイトルを獲得した。

en: to focus attention closely on a particular person, thing, or target
ex: Detectives quickly zeroed in on the victim's business partner as the main suspect.
exJa: 刑事たちはすぐに被害者のビジネスパートナーを主要な容疑者として絞り込んだ。

ja: 行き詰まらせる、停滞させる
en: to cause something to be delayed or stuck, so it cannot make progress
ex: The peace talks got bogged down in arguments over the exact location of the border.
exJa: 和平交渉は国境の正確な位置をめぐる議論で行き詰まった。

en: to start working seriously and with determination
ex: With only a month until the exam, she finally buckled down and studied every evening.
exJa: 試験まで1か月となり、彼女はようやく本腰を入れて毎晩勉強した。

en: to add a comment to a conversation, often in agreement
ex: When I mentioned the new ramen shop, several coworkers chimed in to recommend it too.
exJa: 新しいラーメン屋の話をすると、同僚数人も口々に勧めてきた。

en: to suddenly refuse to speak, from nervousness or to keep a secret
ex: As soon as the detective asked about that night, the witness clammed up and demanded a lawyer.
exJa: 刑事がその夜のことを尋ねるとすぐ、証人は口を閉ざし弁護士を要求した。

en: to appear or happen suddenly and unexpectedly
ex: I had planned to leave early, but a problem cropped up at work and I stayed until nine.
exJa: 早めに帰るつもりだったが、仕事で問題が持ち上がり9時まで残った。

en: to try hard to get support, interest, or business
ex: The candidates toured rural towns to drum up support ahead of the election.
exJa: 候補者たちは選挙を前に支持を集めるため地方の町を回った。

ja: 肉付けする、具体化する
en: to add more details to a plan, idea, or story
ex: The writers need to flesh out the villain's backstory so that viewers understand his motives.
exJa: 脚本家たちは視聴者が動機を理解できるよう、悪役の過去を肉付けする必要がある。

ja: 食いつぶす、がつがつ食べる
en: to use up or take over something quickly; to eat quickly
ex: Rising rents are gobbling up a larger share of young people's income every year.
exJa: 家賃の上昇が年々若者の収入のより大きな割合を食いつぶしている。

en: to pass something to a younger generation; to announce a legal decision
ex: The recipe for this soup has been handed down in my family for four generations.
exJa: このスープのレシピは私の家族で4世代にわたって受け継がれてきた。

en: to show too much respect or obedience to someone powerful
ex: The editor refused to kowtow to advertisers who demanded that negative stories be removed.
exJa: 編集長は否定的な記事を削除するよう求める広告主に屈しなかった。

ja: 鵜呑みにする、喜んで受け入れる
en: to accept or enjoy something eagerly, often without questioning it
ex: The audience lapped up every word of the charismatic speaker's outrageous claims.
exJa: 聴衆はカリスマ的な講演者の突拍子もない主張を一言残らず鵜呑みにした。

ja: （難しいことを）やってのける
en: to succeed in doing something difficult or unexpected
ex: Nobody believed the underdogs could win, but they pulled off a stunning upset against the champions.
exJa: 誰も格下チームが勝つとは信じていなかったが、彼らは王者相手に見事な番狂わせを演じた。

ja: （得点・借金などを）積み重ねる
en: to gradually collect a large amount of points, debts, or profits
ex: He racked up huge credit card debts by buying designer clothes he couldn't afford.
exJa: 彼は買えもしないブランド服を買って、多額のクレジットカードの借金を抱え込んだ。

en: to come together to support someone who is in difficulty
ex: When the restaurant owner fell ill, the whole neighborhood rallied around to keep the business open.
exJa: レストランの店主が病に倒れると、近所の人々が団結して店の営業を支えた。

en: to search quickly through something, often in order to steal
ex: The burglars rifled through every drawer in the house but found nothing of value.
exJa: 泥棒たちは家中の引き出しを片っ端から物色したが、価値のある物は何も見つからなかった。

en: to manage to collect enough money or people, with difficulty
ex: The band scraped together enough money to record their first album in a friend's garage.
exJa: バンドは友人のガレージで最初のアルバムを録音するのに十分なお金をなんとかかき集めた。

ja: 念入りに調べる、選り分ける
en: to examine a large amount of material carefully to find something
ex: Rescue workers sifted through the rubble in search of survivors after the earthquake.
exJa: 地震の後、救助隊員たちは生存者を探してがれきの中を丹念に調べた。

en: to work less hard or with less effort than usual
ex: Sales dropped sharply after the staff started slacking off while the manager was on leave.
exJa: 店長が休暇中にスタッフが手を抜き始めた後、売り上げは急落した。

en: to make a problem or disagreement seem less serious so people can move on
ex: She invited both colleagues to lunch in an effort to smooth over their quarrel.
exJa: 彼女は二人の同僚の口論を丸く収めようと、二人を昼食に誘った。

en: to get money or food from others without working or paying for it
ex: At thirty-five, he still sponges off his parents and shows no interest in finding a job.
exJa: 35歳にもなって彼はまだ親のすねをかじり、仕事を探す気もない。

ja: 偶然見つける、出くわす
en: to find something or meet someone by chance
ex: While cleaning the attic, we stumbled upon a box of letters our grandfather had written during the war.
exJa: 屋根裏を掃除していて、祖父が戦時中に書いた手紙の箱を偶然見つけた。

ja: しまい込む、（目立たない所に）ある
en: to put something in a safe or hidden place; to be located somewhere quiet
ex: The best sushi restaurant in town is tucked away in a narrow alley behind the station.
exJa: 町一番の寿司屋は駅裏の細い路地にひっそりとある。

ja: 要するに～ということになる
en: to have something as the main or most basic point
ex: In the end, the whole argument boils down to a question of who will pay for the repairs.
exJa: 結局のところ、議論全体は誰が修理費を払うのかという問題に尽きる。

ja: （人が）～に気づく、わかってくる
en: to become clear to someone for the first time
ex: Halfway to the airport, it suddenly dawned on me that I had left my passport in the hotel safe.
exJa: 空港へ向かう途中で、ホテルの金庫にパスポートを置いてきたことに突然気づいた。

ja: （計画などが）立ち消えになる
en: to fail to happen or be completed as planned
ex: The sale of our house fell through at the last minute when the buyer couldn't get a mortgage.
exJa: 買い手が住宅ローンを組めなかったため、家の売却は土壇場で立ち消えになった。

ja: ～次第である、～にかかっている
en: to depend completely on something
ex: The success of the whole project hinges on whether we can secure funding by March.
exJa: プロジェクト全体の成否は、3月までに資金を確保できるかどうかにかかっている。

en: to accept an opportunity or offer eagerly
ex: When the publisher offered her a contract for a second novel, she jumped at the chance.
exJa: 出版社から2作目の小説の契約を持ちかけられると、彼女はその機会に飛びついた。

en: to suddenly have a good idea or discover a solution
ex: After weeks of failed experiments, the researchers hit upon a simple solution to the problem.
exJa: 何週間も実験に失敗した後、研究者たちはその問題の簡単な解決策を思いついた。

en: to say something suddenly and without thinking about the effect
ex: Before I could stop him, my son blurted out that we had forgotten Grandma's birthday.
exJa: 止める間もなく、息子は私たちがおばあちゃんの誕生日を忘れていたことを口走った。

en: to delay doing something until later
ex: We decided to hold off on buying a new car until interest rates come down a little.
exJa: 金利が少し下がるまで新車の購入を見合わせることにした。

en: to survive a difficult period or situation without serious harm
ex: Small businesses with cash reserves were better able to ride out the economic downturn.
exJa: 現金の蓄えがある中小企業は、景気低迷をより上手く乗り切ることができた。

en: to keep strong feelings hidden instead of expressing them
ex: He bottled up his grief for years, refusing to talk about his wife's death with anyone.
exJa: 彼は何年も悲しみを胸にしまい込み、妻の死について誰とも話そうとしなかった。

ja: 見下した話し方をする
en: to speak to someone as if they were less intelligent or important than you
ex: Good teachers never talk down to their students, even when explaining the simplest ideas.
exJa: 良い教師は、最も単純な考えを説明するときでも決して生徒を見下した話し方をしない。

ja: 突き止める、確約させる
en: to identify something exactly; to make someone give a clear decision
ex: Engineers are still trying to pin down the exact cause of last night's power outage.
exJa: 技術者たちは昨夜の停電の正確な原因をまだ突き止めようとしている。

ja: 鎮圧する、（火・命を）消す
en: to stop or end something completely, especially by force
ex: The military regime quickly snuffed out the student uprising in the capital, arresting hundreds.
exJa: 軍事政権は首都での学生蜂起を素早く鎮圧し、数百人を逮捕した。
